result.summary:
STEP 0.5 REGISTRY LOOKUP -- NO PRIOR MATCH FOUND. Command run: grep -rniE "NOTIFY|LISTEN|PubSub|polling.vs.push|poll.*push|push.*poll" docs/issues/*.yaml (case-insensitive, on the ISSUE REGISTRY specifically, not lib/). 6 files matched: ISS-0430.yaml (this issue itself), ISS-0421.yaml, ISS-0425.yaml, ISS-0431.yaml, ISS-0213.yaml, ISS-0015.yaml. Checked each of the other 5 individually: ISS-0421 (status: resolved) and ISS-0425 (status: open), ISS-0213 (status: resolved), ISS-0015 (status: resolved) all matched only on the word 'poll' inside unrelated prose (Poller/polling-loop mentions with no NOTIFY/LISTEN/PubSub content) -- none discusses Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY or a push-vs-poll design tradeoff. ISS-0431.yaml (status: resolved, WF02-REQ218-20260903, admission-control/backpressure) is the only substantive hit: its SCOPE section says 'Poller's per-tenant sweeps and future LISTEN/NOTIFY work (ISS-0430) are secondary surfaces to cover by the same decision' and its resolution's disclosed-residual note repeats 'One disclosed residual: ISS-0430's future LISTEN/NOTIFY work ... remains unaddressed -- out of scope for REQ-216/217/218'. This is a FORWARD REFERENCE to the present issue (ISS-0430), not a prior resolution of it -- ISS-0431 explicitly declined to decide the NOTIFY/LISTEN question and deferred it here. CONCLUSION: no prior resolved/instrumented/no_defect issue-registry entry has ever settled or even substantively discussed the NOTIFY/LISTEN/PubSub design question. This is confirmed as the first real design pass on it, consistent with the issue's own lib/-wide grep finding zero usage. Not a recurrence.

STEP (2) POLLER MECHANICS, PULLED DIRECT FROM SOURCE.

Letflow.Scheduler.Poller (lib/letflow/scheduler/poller.ex, backed by Letflow.Scheduler context, lib/letflow/scheduler.ex): poll interval accessor is Letflow.Scheduler.poll_interval_ms/0 (lib/letflow/scheduler.ex:534-537): `def poll_interval_ms do scheduler_config()[:poll_interval_ms] || @default_poll_interval_ms end`, where `@default_poll_interval_ms 5_000` (line 90, i.e. 5000ms/5s default) and `scheduler_config` reads `Application.get_env(:letflow, :scheduler, [])` -- so the config key is the `:poll_interval_ms` key inside the `:scheduler` Application env keyword list (e.g. `config :letflow, scheduler: [poll_interval_ms: N]`). Poller.init/1 schedules its first :tick with Process.send_after(self(), :tick, 0) (poller.ex:212-213) -- zero delay, catch-up-on-restart semantics, no startup-sweep lock. Every subsequent tick reschedules via poller.ex:439-440: `delay = Scheduler.poll_interval_ms() + jitter_extra_ms(); Process.send_after(self(), :tick, delay)` -- jitter (Scheduler.jitter_ms/0, default @default_jitter_ms 0) is added on top of the base interval, not instead of it. Claim query is Letflow.Scheduler.claim_due_timer_ids/2 (scheduler.ex:223-238): `Timer |> where([t], t.status == "pending" and t.fire_at <= ^now) |> order_by([t], asc: t.fire_at) |> limit(^limit) |> select([t], t.id) |> lock("FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED") |> Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema)` -- single-table lock (no join), `limit` from Scheduler.max_timers_per_cycle/0 (default @default_max_timers_per_cycle 64), and `prefix: tenant_schema` is the per-tenant-schema iteration point: the Poller calls this once per tenant schema per tick (per-tenant sweep), each call scoped to exactly one Postgres schema via Ecto's :prefix option.

Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher.Poller (lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher/poller.ex, backed by Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcher context, lib/letflow/engine/service_task_dispatcher.ex): poll interval accessor is ServiceTaskDispatcher.poll_interval_ms/0 (service_task_dispatcher.ex:252-255): `def poll_interval_ms do dispatcher_config()[:poll_interval_ms] || @default_poll_interval_ms end`, where `@default_poll_interval_ms 5_000` (line 100, same 5000ms/5s default as Scheduler.Poller) and `dispatcher_config` reads `Application.get_env(:letflow, :service_task_dispatcher, [])` -- a SEPARATE config key namespace from Scheduler's (`:service_task_dispatcher` vs `:scheduler`), deliberately independent per the module's own moduledoc ('REQ-214's own text is explicit the two pollers are independent concerns with independent poll cadences'). Poller.init/1 likewise schedules its first :tick at zero delay (poller.ex:55-56) and reschedules via poller.ex:97-98: `delay = ServiceTaskDispatcher.poll_interval_ms() + jitter_extra_ms(); Process.send_after(self(), :tick, delay)`. Claim query is ServiceTaskDispatcher.claim_due_dispatch_ids/2 (service_task_dispatcher.ex:437-461), a two-step select-then-lock (deliberately reworked at CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's request to avoid FOR UPDATE OF ambiguity): step 1 is an UNLOCKED joined query -- `ServiceTaskDispatch |> join(:inner, [d], p in InstanceProjection, on: p.instance_id == d.instance_id) |> where([d, p], d.status == "pending" and d.next_attempt_at <= ^now and p.status == :active) |> order_by([d], asc: d.next_attempt_at) |> limit(^limit) |> select([d], d.id) |> Repo.all(prefix: tenant_schema)`; step 2 locks only the id list, single-table, no join: `ServiceTaskDispatch |> where([d], d.id in ^eligible_ids) |> select([d], d.id) |> lock("FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED") |> Repo.all(prefix: tenant_schema)`. `limit` from ServiceTaskDispatcher.max_dispatches_per_cycle/0 (default @default_max_dispatches_per_cycle 64, same 64-row cap as Scheduler). Both queries are `prefix: tenant_schema`-scoped -- same per-tenant-schema iteration point as Scheduler.Poller: poll_and_dispatch/1 is called once per tenant schema per tick.

SUPERVISION PLACEMENT (context for design question 1, connection ownership): both Poller GenServers are children of Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers (lib/letflow/supervisor/pollers.ex), itself a child of the top-level Letflow.Supervisor (lib/letflow/application.ex) alongside Letflow.Supervisor.Infrastructure (which owns Letflow.Repo, first child, and all 17 other infra processes -- see infrastructure.ex), Letflow.Supervisor.PollersBreaker, and Letflow.Supervisor.Http, in that list order. Infrastructure starts and fully completes before Pollers starts (application.ex's own ordering comment, ISS-0429/ISS-0451). Pollers' own child_spec is `restart: :temporary` at the top level (ISS-0451) -- the top-level Letflow.Supervisor never auto-restarts Letflow.Supervisor.Pollers for any exit; PollersBreaker is the sole restarter. Within Pollers, the two poller GenServers are :one_for_one peers with max_restarts: 5, max_seconds: 60 (looser than OTP default, to tolerate transient per-tick faults).

STEP (3) DECISION 0003 DIMENSION B, VERBATIM QUOTE.

docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md, Dimension B heading text (line 39, decision statement): "B -- Multi-tenancy representation: schema-per-tenant, following R-Co's actual current implementation -- not the adp-0x docs' tenant-column-only description taken in isolation. Letflow adopts Postgres schema-per-tenant as the tenant-isolation mechanism, implemented via Ecto's `:prefix` / dynamic-repo query-prefixing support, with `tenant_id` columns retained inside each schema on the tables the adp-0x docs describe, kept as an intra-schema invariant/query-predicate discipline rather than as the isolation boundary itself. This explicitly follows R-Co's actual, current, two-layer implementation (schema-per-tenant + intra-schema `tenant_id`), not the adp-0x docs' original, now-superseded tenant-column-only proposal." And its own concrete Ecto-mechanics text (lines 216-225): "Concrete Ecto/Postgres mechanics of option (b): schema-per-tenant maps to Ecto's `Ecto.Repo` query-`:prefix` support (`Repo.all(query, prefix: tenant_schema)`, or a `prefix/1` callback on affected schemas) -- Ecto has first-class support for Postgres-schema-based multi-tenancy this way, materially different plumbing than a `tenant_id` `WHERE`-clause library. This requires a migration-runner change beyond a single `mix ecto.migrate` run: a `tenant_schemas`-equivalent registry and a provisioning path ... are needed at S2/S3 execution time ... `tenant_id` columns remain plain Ecto fields on schemas that need the intra-schema predicate, no different from a normal column." This is the exact mechanism CODE-DESIGNER must reconcile a database-global NOTIFY channel against: tenant isolation here is a PHYSICAL Postgres-schema boundary enforced per-query via the `:prefix` option passed to Repo.all/Repo.update_all/etc (as both Pollers' own claim queries above literally do, `prefix: tenant_schema`) -- not a `tenant_id` WHERE-predicate library, and NOT anything connection-level (no session-GUC tenant context; decision 0003's own Addendum 2026-08-17 explicitly rejected building one). A `LISTEN`/`NOTIFY` channel is a database-global namespace with no `:prefix` concept at all -- Postgres does not scope LISTEN/NOTIFY by schema or search_path -- so nothing about this isolation mechanism carries over to a NOTIFY channel by default; the design must state its own separate mechanism for preventing a payload/routing-hint issued from within one tenant's schema context from reaching a listener that is not entitled to that tenant's data, since the schema-per-tenant `:prefix` boundary this decision establishes for ordinary queries does not apply to NOTIFY at all.

No file under lib/letflow/design/ was written. No implementation code was written or changed. This is diagnosis/evidence-gathering only.
